extracted.intended_audience: general readers and people interested in graphic/book cover design, publishing, and Chip Kidd's work
extracted.subtask_description: Design principles and practical process guidance for creating book covers, distilled from Chip Kidd's statements and career practices as described in a Wikipedia biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a single signature look
rubrics_metrics.description: A signature look is crippling; the simplest and most effective solutions aren't dictated by style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impose a personal 'house style' across all projects. Tailor the visual approach to each book rather than forcing a recurring, identifiable brand aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be inspired by the book/manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: For the most part I'm inspired by whatever the book is, or by the manuscript itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start design work with a close reading of the manuscript; the content should drive imagery, tone, and concept rather than outside trends or designer ego.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author collaboration and deference
rubrics_metrics.description: After closely reading the work he contacts the author, who 'has final say, so it's a logical starting point.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage the author early, involve them in discussions, and respect their ultimate authority on the cover; use author input as a key decision factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visually solve a problem
rubrics_metrics.description: The work always amounts to: visually solving a problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach cover design as a problem-solving task (communicating theme, audience, tone, distinguishing the book on shelf) rather than purely decorative work; evaluate solutions by how well they solve the communication challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative, sometimes slow development
rubrics_metrics.description: This solution can take up to six months to find.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for concept development and iteration; expect extended exploration and refinement rather than immediate fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collaborators and varied resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Along the way, I may or may not involve photographers or illustrators or any amount of ephemeral detritus that washes up on my shores in the pursuit of solving the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to bringing in photographers, illustrators, found imagery, typographers, and other unexpected resources; mix media and contributors as needed to achieve the concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't overstate the cover's power to sell
rubrics_metrics.description: I'm very much against the idea that the cover will sell the book. ... it's about whether the book itself really connects with the public, and the cover is only a small part of that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design covers to serve and reflect the book rather than treating the cover as the primary marketing lever; avoid making exaggerated claims about cover-driven sales when judging success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create covers that treat books as objects of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers Weekly described his book jackets as 'creepy, striking, sly, smart, unpredictable covers that make readers appreciate books as objects of art as well as literature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the tactile and visual object qualities of the book (cover, jacket, materials) so the design can elevate the book as a physical/art object in addition to conveying literary content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect iconic character/design solutions when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Batman himself is such a brilliant design solution (Kidd's comment on the character's design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with established, iconic subjects (e.g., well-known characters), leverage their intrinsic design strengths and symbolism instead of overwriting them; use iconic elements thoughtfully to connect with existing cultural recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity/throughput as a professional metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Turning out jacket designs at an average of 75 covers a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a professional publishing context, sustaining a high output and meeting publisher schedules is a practical performance criterion; balance creative depth with reliable delivery.
